description: Build .NET applications with multiple AI providers through consistent completion, streaming and tool workflows. Supports OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra/Sol/Luna, Anthropic including Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5, Google, xAI including Grok 4.7, DeepSeek Flash/V4 Pro and Perplexity. Includes immutable request builders, controllable Runs, typed output, cancellable local tools, reasoning, search/citations, image generation/editing, capability inspection and per-request processing-speed observations. Targets .NET Standard 2.1; requires Mythosia.AI.Abstractions 4.2.0. What's New in v8.2.0: GPT-6.1 Sol adds mandatory reasoning, Responses tools and native Run support; Sonnet 5.5 adds adaptive/high defaults and explicit between-tools thinking. Request preparation captures effective settings, runs profile hooks once and validates before side effects. Nested auxiliary requests isolate parent state; forwarded profile changes preserve later request-local tool and policy edits. Claude retains signed and tool history across projection, counting and permitted compaction, preserves persistent instructions, and serializes valid lowercase tool schemas. Streaming fixes cover producer cleanup, HTTP error-body cancellation, identifiable HttpClient timeouts and preservation of outcomes during response disposal. OpenAI Run honors configured endpoints and preserves steering order, cancellation boundaries and terminal outcomes. Existing public execution APIs and service defaults remain. Known limitations: Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5 pauses ending in a pending server_tool_use can be rejected before continuation. Custom buffering HTTP content can delay successful SSE body acquisition past cancellation or timeout, retaining the active Run. These cases remain unfixed. Full release notes: https://github.com/AJ-comp/Mythosia.AI/blob/main/src/core/Mythosia.AI/RELEASE_NOTES.md#v820
releaseNotes: v8.2.0 adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 across completion, streaming, structured output, images, tools, web search and Run. Untouched settings use adaptive/high thinking with readable thinking omitted. ClaudeThinkingMode and WithBetweenToolsThinking add explicit up-front thinking control; None and disabled legacy budgets use high-effort between_tools, which still permits tool progress. Between-tools accepts Auto/Low/Medium/High, omits display/budget/binding fields and rejects per-message effort changes and cache-preserving overrides. Signed empty thinking and progress metadata survive turns and tools; stored assistant edits fail locally, while earlier prefix changes follow provider binding policy; adaptive mode can request Error or DropBlock explicitly. Forced tools, assistant prefills, Minimal, Fast, native async tools and Run steering are unsupported for Sonnet 5.5. Existing model defaults remain. Claude reasoning and binding are resolved together per request. Stateless auxiliary profiles with DisableReasoning enabled and a non-default purpose omit inherited binding; Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1 use Low without readable thinking, and Sonnet 5.5 uses high-effort between_tools. Parent settings/history and public APIs remain unchanged; explicitly stateful requests retain binding and normal validation. Completion, streaming, structured output and Run share one request preparation boundary: capture and install options, execute real virtual profile hooks once, then validate effective common and native settings before automatic summaries, input-history changes or transport startup. Application calls own logical requests even with reused profiles or messages. Framework virtual adapters and their first matching base entry preserve prepared settings when input is replaced; default callback streaming also continues the original request. Ordinary nested context/tool callback calls remain independent. Built-in input snapshots prevent later context and turn instructions from rewriting accepted history; custom content stays owner-managed and shared-conversation concurrency is not enabled. Perplexity validation and serialization share one effective plan, excluding suppressed parent reasoning and tools from auxiliary Sonar validation. Claude summary guards inspect retained canonical wire history, including native, typed, legacy and AdditionalMessages signed thinking. Default binding protects that prefix; explicit DropBlock permits compaction where supported, subject to other conversation constraints. Custom Run sessions retain captured options across initial progress events, and compatibility agent round limits remain local. Known summary cuts preserve surviving Claude occurrences; standalone prompt counting ignores unrelated history. The additive protected ResolveRequestMessage helper supports provider input ownership without changing existing execution signatures. Protected BeginIndependentRequestScope separates an unrelated helper called by an override at the same base entry before forwarding. Await or fully enumerate the helper inside the scope; disposal restores outer settings, features, context and delegation. It does not isolate history or permit concurrency; use a stateless helper profile. Each Run owns a copy of its effective settings after StartRunAsync returns, so caller profile restoration cannot alter the active Run; execution profile hooks still run once. Stateless auxiliary requests isolate parent history, summaries, observations, output schemas and user options without skipping native OpenAI, Perplexity or other provider validation. Stateful requests retain conversation and binding checks. Claude validates the complete effective thinking plan, including consumed manual budgets and undefined effort, before side effects; valid profile/common reasoning overrides retain precedence. Ordinary and preserved Claude history and token counting share one projection. Equivalent defined enum, integer, string and JSON FunctionSource values do not duplicate imported parallel batches or accepted tool calls; signatures, order and provider fields remain. Ordinary requests retain native historical calls/results after functions are disabled or removed. Parameterless token counting includes enabled definitions and tool_choice while retaining historical tool turns when tools are disabled. Standalone prompt counting and count-specific restrictions remain. v8.2.0 also adds GPT-6.1 Sol through existing completion, streaming, structured-output, image-input, tools and Run APIs. Supports Low/Medium/High/XHigh/Max reasoning with Medium default; None/Minimal are rejected. Includes native async tools in Standard/Pro, Standard-only steering, Standard single-agent cache-preserving reasoning updates, Pro and paid Fast processing. Pro Run and functions remain supported; local steering rejection does not abort the run. Run resolves responses against HttpClient.BaseAddress, maps HTTP(S) to WS(S), and rejects invalid bases without endpoint fallback; its dedicated socket and protected transport override remain. Cancelling steering while waiting to send preserves the Run; in-flight send cancellation or failure may abort it. Cancellation while awaiting acknowledgement does not retract sent input. Accepted steering retains its continuation-response position in history when output processing lags. Nonrecoverable Run transport failures cancel cooperative tools and preserve the original failure after cleanup; tools that ignore cancellation are still awaited. Fully received final responses survive normal WebSocket closure when a peer Close frame arrives during completion of their initial or tool-result send, without replay or suppression of caller cancellation or unconfirmed send failures. A received terminal API error retains its original reason across a later close while local tools run. Existing service defaults and GPT-6 Sol/Luna None behavior remain. Requires Mythosia.AI.Abstractions 4.2.0. Full notes: https://github.com/AJ-comp/Mythosia.AI/blob/main/src/core/Mythosia.AI/RELEASE_NOTES.md#v820 Forwarded profile changes replace prior profile flags against captured settings before automatic summary; callback streaming cancels and drains its producer, retains observer and cleanup failures, and uses captured recovery budgets; Claude protects Mythos bound thinking and retained override/tool dependencies, groups additional legacy batches once; stateless OpenAI helpers preserve parent history guards. Profile replacement preserves later tool/policy edits and explicit same-value setting assignments. Allowed Claude compaction retains persistent conversation instructions separately from summaries, in order and with system authority; turn-only scope and failure/cancellation rollback remain. Claude tool schemas use lowercase JSON Schema keywords and recursively map array items, preserving parameter names and default object keys while omitting unset optional fields. Public parameter APIs are unchanged. Anthropic streaming and Run interrupt stalled HTTP error-body reads on cancellation or request-policy timeout, allowing cleanup and later Run reuse. Caller cancellation and policy timeout retain their distinct exception behavior; public APIs are unchanged. Common streaming rounds classify identifiable HttpClient timeouts (TaskCanceledException with an inner TimeoutException) as AIServiceException with the original transport exception retained, so Run.Result faults with its timeout cause. This applies when neither caller cancellation nor the request policy timeout has fired; their behavior and other transport cancellation remain unchanged. Claude streaming and Run await asynchronous cleanup of acquired HTTP response bodies. Subsequent response/content disposal failures do not replace successful completion, the original read error or cancellation; disposal of the original response/content is still attempted. Known limitations in v8.2.0: Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5 pause_turn responses ending in a pending server_tool_use can be rejected as assistant prefill before continuation; completion, streaming and Run are affected, while completed-server-result pauses still continue. Custom buffering HttpContent can hold successful SSE body acquisition past caller cancellation or a request-policy timeout, retaining the active-Run guard. Ordinary SocketsHttpHandler streaming and the corrected HTTP error-body path passed local checks. Both cases remain unfixed. These latest lifecycle fixes were validated with deterministic tests and local HTTP connections, not live provider API calls. Details: https://github.com/AJ-comp/Mythosia.AI/blob/main/src/core/Mythosia.AI/RELEASE_NOTES.md#known-limitations
